newsitem.title: MALI: Two killed in Mali poll violence -- state TV.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Mali poll violence -- state TV.

text.p: Two people were killed during violence linked to Mali's rerun parliamentary election on Sunday, state television reported.
The two men died in the radical opposition stronghold of San, east of the capital, it said. It did not specify whether they were opposition militants or ordinary people.

The radical opposition boycotted the poll as part of a campaign to force President Alpha Oumar Konare to scrap and reschedule the former French colony's second multi-party elections. Witnesses said turnout appeared low.
Polling in the capital Bamako was peaceful but state radio and witnesses reported polling stations and cars being ransacked or set ablaze in other opposition strongholds upcountry.
Mali was one of the stars of Africa's 1990s democracy movement. The constitutional court scrapped the original parliamentary election on April 13, citing chaos and irregularities.

The opposition wanted the whole election timetable revised but Konare, a historian elected in 1992, pressed ahead with only minor modifications. He won a new five-year term on May 11. The main opposition boycotted that election.
